title: Tech Note: Keeping the Memory Clean - Part 2

historical_commentary.text: This note is Part 2 of a two-part series teaching developers how to write 4D code that keeps RAM 'clean' to preserve application performance and stability, a critical concern in the era of limited RAM on classic Mac OS/Windows systems; the specific memory-management coding tricks described are obsolete since modern 4D and modern hardware/OS memory management have changed the relevant constraints dramatically, though the general engineering discipline of being mindful of memory usage remains a timeless principle.
related_updates: Modern computers have vastly more RAM and modern 4D versions include substantially improved automatic memory management compared to the constrained classic Mac OS/Windows 3.1/95 environments this note addresses
Specific 1997-era memory-cleaning coding tricks are no longer necessary or applicable given decades of evolution in both 4D's internal memory handling and underlying OS memory management
